newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIA LATE PALM OLEIN STABLE, EYES ON RUPIAH.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIA LATE PALM OLEIN STABLE, EYES ON RUPIAH.

text.p: Indonesian palm olein prices remained generally stable in late trading on Wednesday on average demand as players kept their eyes on the rupiah's decline against the U.S. dollar, traders said.
They said palm olein was quoted unchanged at 1,495-1,500 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, around the same as Tuesday's close. Trades earlier in the day had also been heard at 1,485-90 rupiah.
Crude palm oil was done at 1,246 rupiah/kg in the Sumatran city of Medan on Tuesday, but there were no tenders.
"Like in Malaysia, where palm olein rose after the ringgit fell, we expect local palm olein to go up if the rupiah continues to fall," one Jakarta trader said.
Traders described volume as average, with the market said to be taking a wait-and-see position amid the volative currencies.
They said export prices remained attractive despite slight declines in European prices overnight. September palm olein was down $2.50 at $525 in Europe.
Any fall in the Indonesian currency against the U.S. dollar would improve export competitiveness, they added.
